title: From consultation to neat, comfortable cornrows

say: From consultation to neat, comfortable cornrows.
This is the video for module two of Hair Care and Simple Styling.
Good stylists ask the right questions first, so there are no surprises. Ask what style, size and length she wants, and agree what is realistic for her hair.

panel.heading: Five consultation questions
items: What style, size and length do you want?
When was your last chemical service?
Any allergies, scalp conditions or sore areas?
How long do you plan to keep it?
Price, extension hair and hours: agreed

say: Ask about her last relaxer, colour or keratin treatment. A chemical service in the last two weeks changes what is safe.

say: Start with clean, moisturised, stretched hair, and the client's head at your chest height.
Step one. With the comb tail, part a straight line from the hairline to the nape, then a second line parallel to it. Clip the rest away.

panel.heading: Braiding one all-back row
items: Part two straight lines, front to nape
Add a little gel or cream for grip
Take a small piece, split into three strands
Cross left under middle, then right under
Add loose hair to the outer strand each time
Hands close to the scalp, all the way down

say: Step two. A little gel or braiding cream along the row controls frizz and gives grip.

panel.heading: Braiding one all-back row
items: Part two straight lines, front to nape
Add a little gel or cream for grip
Take a small piece, split into three strands
Cross left under middle, then right under
Add loose hair to the outer strand each time
Hands close to the scalp, all the way down

say: Step three. At the hairline, take a small piece and divide it into three equal strands.

say: Step four. Cross the left strand under the middle, then the right strand under the new middle. This underhand method makes the classic raised cornrow.

say: Step five. Before each cross, pick up a little loose hair from the row with your index finger and add it to the outer strand.

say: Keep those amounts small and equal. Picking up too much is why rows get wider towards the nape.

say: Step six. Keep your knuckles close to the scalp to avoid gaps and loops. At the nape, finish with a normal three-strand braid and secure the end.

say: A cornrow should feel snug. Pull hardest in the middle of the head, and be gentlest at the hairline and temples, where hair is finest.

panel.heading: Firm, never painful
left: Firmest in the middle of the head

say: If she winces, if you see small white bumps, or the scalp lifts like a tent around the braid, it is too tight. Loosen it.
Repeated tight styling can cause traction alopecia, hair loss from constant pulling, which can become permanent.

panel.heading: Firm, never painful
left: Firmest in the middle of the head

say: For example, Halima in Kano has a client at 10 a.m. for medium knotless braids. Consultation and scalp check take 10 minutes.

say: Check the hairline, crown and nape in good light. If you see signs of infection, open sores or a recent chemical burn, do not continue. Suggest a clinic.

cards.d: Infection, open sores or a fresh chemical burn: do not continue. Suggest a clinic.
Hot water in a stable bowl, never the kettle over her. Blot with a towel, keep it off the skin.
Bigger, lighter styles, short breaks, no relaxers. If she cries from pain, loosen it.

say: When you seal synthetic ends, dip them in hot water from a stable bowl, never from a kettle held over the client, then blot with a towel.

say: With children, the parent consults and the child's comfort comes first. Choose bigger, lighter styles. If a child cries from pain, the braid is too tight.

say: It's fine teaches you nothing. After each practice, take photos, time yourself, and score parts, braid size, comfort and ends from 1 to 5.

panel.heading: Your practice feedback loop
items: Do one practice style
Photograph and time it
Score parts, size, comfort, ends: 1 to 5
Fix one weak point
Practise again

say: For example, Rukayat in Abeokuta scored her parts 2 out of 5. She practised parting on a mannequin for 20 minutes a day. In three sessions her total rose from 12 to 17 out of 20, and she saved an hour.

say: To remember. Consult and write a card every time. Stretch before parting. Pick up small, equal amounts for even rows. Firm but never painful. And fix one weak point at a time.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Every service starts with a consultation card
Stretch coily hair before you part it
Small, equal pick-ups give even rows
Firm but not painful; gentlest at the edges
Fix one weak point at a time

say: Now practise. Run one real consultation, braid a full all-back with a comfort rating, and score a section of twists or box braids.
